expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint rather than rewriting the server
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses the bug ('single-threaded accept loop calling handle(conn) synchronously') and gives a minimal fix — a 7-line accept-loop snippet with 'go handle(conn)' — plus two hints (sync.RWMutex, mutex for AOF writes); no full server rewrite.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: No runnable checkpoint with expected output/behaviour. Only 'Run with `go run -race .` to catch them' — a diagnostic suggestion with no expected output, and no command like 'connect two redis-cli clients and expect both to get replies'.

expectations.text: B3: Identifies that handle(conn) blocks the accept loop and must run concurrently (e.g. `go handle(conn)`) or use an event loop
expectations.evidence: '`handle(conn)` runs inline in the accept loop, so the loop stays inside `handle` until the first client disconnects. Only then does control return to `Accept()`' and fix 'go handle(conn)'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0), SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0); only tool call is glob {"pattern": "**/*.go"}. No install commands, nothing outside the workspace.
